stemMd: Why does the curator call the decision a compromise?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It leaves the near-fall problem entirely unchanged

options.label: B
options.textMd: It improves access while losing part of the threshold’s original experience

options.label: C
options.textMd: It preserves every aspect of the original use exactly

options.label: D
options.textMd: It makes the new slab older than the old one

options.label: E
options.textMd: It rejects the value of historical material

explanationMd: The decision addresses a practical access problem but changes how visitors encounter the historic stone. Keeping the material in a case cannot reproduce walking over it. Both benefit and loss are acknowledged.

distractorRationale.a: The slab was replaced to address that problem.
distractorRationale.c: The text explicitly denies complete preservation.
distractorRationale.e: The old slab was deliberately retained.
distractorRationale.d: The compromise concerns values, not impossible chronology.
